name: Le Neuf
description: Le Neuf ('Nines') is a French-Canadian trick-taking game from Quebec/Acadian communities. 3 players (4-player variant exists). 52-card deck, 13 each + 13-card 'Chômeur' spare hand. Start at 9 points, subtract to 0. Quota = 4 tricks: each trick above -1pt, below +1pt. Rotating trump cycle: Hearts-Diamonds-Clubs-Spades-No Trump. Can swap hand with Chômeur.

history.origins: Le Neuf is a trick-taking game from Eastern Canada, played mainly in French-speaking Quebec (as Le Neuf or Chômeur) and by Acadians in Nova Scotia, and in Newfoundland and Eastern Ontario under the name Nines. It belongs to the quota-whist family; the name refers to each player starting with 9 points.
timeline: 20th century: Played in Quebec, Acadian regions and Newfoundland (Eastern Canada).
history.cultural: Popular in Quebec and Acadian communities.

rules.objective: Reach a score of zero by making more than your quota of four tricks per deal; each extra trick subtracts one point, each trick below quota adds one point.
rules.gameplay: Rotating trumps: ♥-♦-♣-♠-NT cycle. May swap entire hand with Chômeur (first refusal passes right). Follow suit, trump if void. Quota=4 tricks: above=-1pt, below=+1pt. Win all 13=instant win (-9pts).

tips: Watch the Chômeur hand exposed before deciding to swap.
Remember the rotating trump cycle to plan ahead.
Track tricks taken vs. quota of 4 to manage score changes.
Attempting to win all 13 tricks gives instant -9 victory.

scoring.description: Start at 9. Tricks above 4: -1pt each. Below 4: +1pt each. First to 0 wins.
scoring.winCondition: First to reduce score from 9 to 0.
